{
  "approach": "query",
  "change": "Refactor db.py to use parameterized SQL queries for filtering instead of loading all rows into memory. Specifically: 1) In list_notes, replace the full table scan with a SQL query using LIKE for search_text and a generated WHERE clause for tags_filter (using JSON_CONTAINS or LIKE on the tags column). 2) In get_note, replace the full table scan with a direct SELECT WHERE id = ?. 3) In update_note, replace the full table scan with a direct SELECT WHERE id = ? to check existence. 4) In delete_note, replace the full table scan with a direct DELETE WHERE id = ? and check affected rows. 5) In create_note, replace the full table scan with a direct SELECT WHERE id = lastrowid.",
  "hypothesis": "The current implementation performs full table scans (SELECT * FROM notes) for every read operation, including single-note lookups and list queries, regardless of filters. This results in O(N) time complexity for all reads, where N is the total number of notes. By using parameterized SQL queries with WHERE clauses, we reduce the complexity to O(1) for single-note lookups and O(K) for list queries (where K is the number of matching notes), significantly reducing CPU time spent on data transfer, JSON parsing, and Python-side filtering. The profile shows high cumulative time in _to_note and list_notes, which will be reduced by fetching only relevant rows.",
  "risks": [
    "Incorrect SQL syntax for tag filtering may lead to incorrect results or errors.",
    "SQL injection if parameterization is not used correctly (mitigated by using ? placeholders).",
    "Performance regression if the database is very small and query overhead exceeds full scan cost (unlikely given the profile data).",
    "Changes to query logic must preserve exact sorting (ORDER BY id ASC) and filtering semantics (case-sensitive substring search, exact tag matching)."
  ],
  "schema_version": 1,
  "used_memory": []
}
